children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.multidisciplinary
children.doc:
Multidisciplinary problem presets.

Covers cross-domain PDE and ODE problems spanning climate science, materials
discovery, finance, pharmacokinetics, and social systems.

Each preset returns a ``ProblemSpec`` ready for use with the pinneapple
training pipeline, data generation, and digital twin modules.

Domains
-------
Climate Modeling
  - climate_atmosphere_2d   : 2D shallow water equations (atmospheric dynamics)
  - climate_ocean_gyre      : Ocean gyre circulation (Stommel beta-plane model)

Material Discovery
  - crystal_phonon          : 1D phonon Boltzmann transport (lattice temperature)
  - material_fracture_2d    : Phase-field fracture model 2D (Cahn-Hilliard + elasticity)

Financial Modeling
  - black_scholes_1d        : Black-Scholes PDE for option pricing (1D in S)
  - heston_pde_2d           : Heston stochastic volatility PDE (2D in S, v)

Pharmacokinetics
  - pk_two_compartment      : Two-compartment PK ODE system
  - drug_diffusion_tissue   : Drug diffusion and metabolism in 2D tissue

Social Systems
  - sir_epidemic            : SIR epidemic ODE system
  - opinion_dynamics_2d     : 2D spatial opinion dynamics PDE

functions.name: climate_atmosphere_2d
functions.sig: (g: float = 9.81, f: float = 0.0001, H0: float = 1000.0, U_ref: float = 10.0, lon_min: float = 0.0, lon_max: float = 360.0, lat_min: float = -90.0, lat_max: float = 90.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D shallow water equations for atmospheric dynamics.

PDE (nonlinear, rotating form on an f-plane — f is a constant
mid-latitude Coriolis parameter, not a function of latitude):
    ∂h/∂t + ∂(hu)/∂x + ∂(hv)/∂y = 0
    ∂u/∂t + u ∂u/∂x + v ∂u/∂y - f v + g ∂h/∂x = 0
    ∂v/∂t + u ∂v/∂x + v ∂v/∂y + f u + g ∂h/∂y = 0

Fields: h (fluid height/geopotential), u (east-west velocity), v (north-south velocity).

Parameters
----------
g      : gravitational acceleration (m/s²)
f      : Coriolis parameter (s⁻¹); mid-latitude approximation
H0     : reference layer thickness (m)
U_ref  : reference wind speed (m/s)
lon_min/lon_max : longitude bounds (degrees)
lat_min/lat_max : latitude bounds (degrees)

functions.name: climate_ocean_gyre
functions.sig: (beta: float = 2e-11, tau0: float = 0.1, r: float = 1e-07, rho0: float = 1025.0, H: float = 500.0, L: float = 1000000.0, W: float = 500000.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Ocean gyre circulation — Stommel beta-plane model.

Stommel model PDE (for barotropic streamfunction psi):
    r ∇²ψ + β ∂ψ/∂x = (1/ρ₀ H) curl(τ)

where curl(τ) is the wind-stress curl (prescribed forcing).
Fields: psi (barotropic streamfunction, m²/s).

Parameters
----------
beta  : planetary vorticity gradient β = df/dy (m⁻¹ s⁻¹)
tau0  : wind stress amplitude (N/m²)
r     : Rayleigh bottom friction coefficient (s⁻¹)
rho0  : reference ocean density (kg/m³)
H     : layer depth (m)
L     : zonal basin width (m)
W     : meridional basin width (m)

functions.name: crystal_phonon
functions.sig: (k: float = 150.0, tau: float = 1e-12, vg: float = 3000.0, T_hot: float = 320.0, T_cold: float = 280.0, L_domain: float = 1e-06) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Phonon transport / lattice dynamics in 1D — simplified Boltzmann transport.

Simplified phonon BTE (gray approximation):
    ∂T/∂t + vg ∂T/∂x = -(T - T_eq) / tau + k/Cv ∂²T/∂x²

where T is the lattice temperature and the equation reduces in steady-state
to a diffusion-relaxation balance that captures ballistic-to-diffusive
crossover in nanoscale crystals.

Fields: T (lattice temperature, K).

Parameters
----------
k   : effective thermal conductivity (W/m·K)
tau : phonon relaxation time (s)
vg  : phonon group velocity (m/s)
T_hot/T_cold : boundary temperatures (K)
L_domain : sample length (m)

functions.name: material_fracture_2d
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, Gc: float = 2700.0, l0: float = 0.005, Lx: float = 1.0, Ly: float = 1.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Phase-field fracture model 2D — Bourdin-Francfort-Marigo formulation.

Coupled PDEs:
    Elasticity:  div[ (1-phi)² C : eps(u) ] = 0
    Phase-field: Gc/l0 * phi - Gc l0 ∇²phi = 2(1-phi) H

where phi in [0,1] is the damage field, H is the crack driving force
(max strain energy history), and C is the elastic stiffness.

Fields: ux (x-displacement), uy (y-displacement), phi (damage field).

Parameters
----------
E   : Young's modulus (Pa)
nu  : Poisson's ratio
Gc  : critical energy release rate / fracture energy (J/m²)
l0  : phase-field regularization length (m)
Lx/Ly : domain dimensions (m)

functions.name: black_scholes_1d
functions.sig: (sigma: float = 0.2, r: float = 0.05, K: float = 100.0, T: float = 1.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Black-Scholes PDE for European call option pricing.

PDE (in forward-time τ = T - t convention):
    ∂V/∂τ = 0.5 σ² S² ∂²V/∂S² + r S ∂V/∂S - r V

Terminal condition (τ=0, i.e. t=T):  V(S, T) = max(S - K, 0)
Boundary conditions:
    V(0, t)  = 0  (worthless at S=0)
    V(S→∞)  ~ S - K e^{-r(T-t)}  (linear for large S, Neumann approx)

Fields: V (option value).

Parameters
----------
sigma : volatility (annualised, dimensionless)
r     : risk-free interest rate (annualised)
K     : strike price
T     : time to maturity (years)

functions.name: heston_pde_2d
functions.sig: (kappa: float = 2.0, theta: float = 0.04, sigma_v: float = 0.3, rho: float = -0.7, r: float = 0.05, K: float = 100.0, T: float = 1.0, S_max: float = 300.0, v_max: float = 1.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Heston stochastic volatility PDE for European option pricing (2D).

PDE (in forward-time τ = T - t):
    ∂V/∂τ = 0.5 S² v ∂²V/∂S²
          + ρ σ_v S v ∂²V/∂S∂v
          + 0.5 σ_v² v ∂²V/∂v²
          + r S ∂V/∂S
          + κ(θ - v) ∂V/∂v
          - r V

Fields: V (option value, function of S, v, tau).

Parameters
----------
kappa   : mean reversion speed of variance
theta   : long-run average variance
sigma_v : vol-of-vol
rho     : correlation between asset and variance Brownian motions
r       : risk-free rate
K       : strike price
T       : maturity (years)
S_max   : maximum asset price in domain
v_max   : maximum variance in domain

functions.name: pk_two_compartment
functions.sig: (k12: float = 0.5, k21: float = 0.3, kel: float = 0.2, V1: float = 10.0, dose: float = 500.0, t_end: float = 24.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Two-compartment pharmacokinetic (PK) model — ODE system.

ODE system:
    dC1/dt = -(k12 + kel) C1 + k21 C2 + dose_rate(t) / V1
    dC2/dt = k12 C1 - k21 C2

where C1 is the drug concentration in the central compartment (blood/plasma)
and C2 is the concentration in the peripheral compartment (tissue).
IV bolus initial conditions: C1(0) = dose / V1, C2(0) = 0.

Fields: C1 (central compartment concentration), C2 (peripheral).

Parameters
----------
k12  : transfer rate central -> peripheral (h⁻¹)
k21  : transfer rate peripheral -> central (h⁻¹)
kel  : elimination rate from central compartment (h⁻¹)
V1   : volume of distribution of central compartment (L)
dose : IV bolus dose (mg)
t_end: simulation end time (h)

functions.name: drug_diffusion_tissue
functions.sig: (D: float = 1e-10, lam: float = 5e-05, C0: float = 1.0, Lx: float = 0.01, Ly: float = 0.005, t_end: float = 3600.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Drug diffusion and first-order metabolism in 2D tissue.

PDE (reaction-diffusion):
    ∂C/∂t = D (∂²C/∂x² + ∂²C/∂y²) - λ C

where C is drug concentration, D is the effective diffusion coefficient
in tissue, and λ is the first-order elimination rate.

Fields: C (drug concentration, e.g. mg/mL or mol/m³).

Parameters
----------
D    : diffusion coefficient (m²/s), typical tissue: 1e-11 to 1e-9 m²/s
lam  : first-order elimination / metabolism rate (s⁻¹)
C0   : initial / inlet concentration (same units as C)
Lx/Ly : tissue domain dimensions (m)
t_end : simulation duration (s)

functions.name: sir_epidemic
functions.sig: (beta: float = 0.3, gamma: float = 0.1, N: float = 1000000.0, I0: float = 100.0, t_end: float = 200.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
SIR epidemic model — ODE system.

ODE system:
    dS/dt = -beta S I / N
    dI/dt =  beta S I / N - gamma I
    dR/dt =  gamma I

with conservation S + I + R = N.

Fields: S (susceptible), I (infected), R (recovered).

Parameters
----------
beta  : effective contact / transmission rate (day⁻¹)
gamma : recovery rate (day⁻¹); mean infectious period = 1/gamma days
N     : total population size
I0    : initial number of infected individuals
t_end : simulation end time (days)

functions.name: opinion_dynamics_2d
functions.sig: (D: float = 0.01, alpha: float = 1.0, Lx: float = 1.0, Ly: float = 1.0, t_end: float = 10.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D spatial opinion dynamics PDE — continuum Hegselmann-Krause model.

PDE (nonlinear reaction-diffusion on opinion field u ∈ [-1, 1]):
    ∂u/∂t = D ∇²u + α f(u)

where f(u) = u(1 - u²) is a bistable reaction term (double-well potential
derivative) that drives opinions toward the extremes ±1, while diffusion
D ∇²u models spatial influence / social interaction across neighbours.

Homogeneous Neumann BCs model a closed society (no opinion flux at boundary).

Fields: u (spatial opinion field, u ∈ [-1, 1]).

Parameters
----------
D      : spatial diffusion coefficient (opinion spread, m²/time)
alpha  : interaction / polarisation strength
Lx/Ly  : spatial domain dimensions
t_end  : simulation end time

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.registry
children.doc:
Registry mapping problem preset names to factory functions.

Usage

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.solid_mechanics
children.doc:
Solid mechanics presets — elasticity, axisymmetric, contact problems.

Covers problems that arise in structural / mechanical engineering:
  - Axisymmetric linear elasticity (hollow cylinders, pressure vessels,
    threaded couplings, shafts, valve seats, …)
  - Thick-walled cylinder under pressure (Lamé — analytical solution available)
  - Parametric threaded connection (e.g. TC50 pin-box coupling)
  - 2D plane strain for cross-sections under plane loading

Convention
----------
  E  : Young's modulus (Pa)
  nu : Poisson's ratio
  lambda = E·nu / ((1+nu)·(1-2ν))   — Lamé first parameter
  mu     = E / (2·(1+nu))             — Lamé second / shear modulus

Axisymmetric (r, z) strain–displacement relations
--------------------------------------------------
  ε_rr = ∂u_r/∂r
  ε_zz = ∂u_z/∂z
  ε_θθ = u_r / r            ← hoop strain
  ε_rz = (∂u_r/∂z + ∂u_z/∂r) / 2

Constitutive (isotropic, small strain)
---------------------------------------
  σ_rr = λ·tr + 2μ·ε_rr
  σ_zz = λ·tr + 2μ·ε_zz
  σ_θθ = λ·tr + 2μ·ε_θθ    (tr = ε_rr + ε_zz + ε_θθ)
  σ_rz = 2μ·ε_rz

Equilibrium (body force = 0)
-----------------------------
  ∂σ_rr/∂r + ∂σ_rz/∂z + (σ_rr − σ_θθ)/r = 0
  ∂σ_rz/∂r + ∂σ_zz/∂z + σ_rz/r          = 0

functions.name: axisymmetric_linear_elasticity_2d_default
functions.sig: (r_min: float = 10.0, r_max: float = 50.0, z_min: float = 0.0, z_max: float = 100.0, E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, p_inner: float = 0.0, p_outer: float = 0.0, traction_z_top: float = 0.0, fix_z_bottom: bool = True, fix_r_inner: bool = False) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D axisymmetric linear elasticity in (r, z) coordinates.

Fields : u_r (radial displacement), u_z (axial displacement)
PDE    : axisymmetric equilibrium — div(σ) = 0 in cylindrical coords
Domain : r ∈ [r_min, r_max], z ∈ [z_min, z_max]

Boundary conditions (all optional, controlled by parameters):
  - u_z = 0 at z = z_min  (fixed base)
  - u_r = 0 at r = r_min  (axis of symmetry OR rigid bore)
  - σ_rr = p_inner at r = r_min (internal pressure)
  - σ_rr = p_outer at r = r_max (external pressure)
  - σ_zz = traction_z_top at z = z_max (axial traction)

Analytical solution available for thick-walled cylinder:
  Use get_preset("thick_walled_cylinder_lame", ...)

Applications
------------
Threaded couplings, pressure vessels, gun barrels, rotating shafts,
valve seats, bearing races, bolted flanges.

functions.name: thick_walled_cylinder_lame_default
functions.sig: (a: float = 20.0, b: float = 60.0, L: float = 100.0, p_a: float = 100000000.0, p_b: float = 0.0, E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Thick-walled hollow cylinder under internal/external pressure (Lamé problem).

Analytical solution (Lamé equations):
  σ_rr(r) = (a²p_a - b²p_b)/(b²-a²)  +  (p_b-p_a)·a²b²/[(b²-a²)·r²]
  σ_θθ(r) = (a²p_a - b²p_b)/(b²-a²)  -  (p_b-p_a)·a²b²/[(b²-a²)·r²]
  u_r(r)  = r/(E(b²-a²)) · [(1-ν)(a²p_a-b²p_b) + (1+ν)a²b²(p_a-p_b)/r²]

Use ``lame_analytical(r, a, b, p_a, p_b, E, nu)`` to evaluate the
ground truth at any radial position.

Applications
------------
Pressure vessels, gun barrels, hydraulic cylinders, thick rings.
Benchmark problem for validating elasticity PINNs.

functions.name: lame_analytical
functions.sig: (r: np.ndarray, a: float, b: float, p_a: float, p_b: float, E: float, nu: float) -> dict
functions.doc:
Lamé analytical solution for thick-walled cylinder.

Parameters
----------
r : array — radial coordinates  (a ≤ r ≤ b)

Returns dict with keys: sigma_rr, sigma_tt, u_r

functions.name: threaded_coupling_tc50_box_default
functions.sig: (clearance: float = 0.1, thread_height: float = 0.8, offset: float = 1.0, E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, traction_top: float = 100000000.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D axisymmetric FEM preset for TC50 threaded coupling BOX body.

Geometry (bounding box, actual profile is complex):
  r ∈ [r_bore, r_outer] = [50.0, 84.15] mm
  z ∈ [0, L_thread + L_shoulder] = [0, 140] mm

The complex threaded profile is handled by the FEM mesh (mesh.msh).
PINNeAPPle uses the bounding box for collocation sampling; actual geometry
constraints come from FEM data or the mesh bridge.

Boundary conditions:
  u_z = 0 at z = 0       — fixed nose (thread start)
  σ_zz = traction_top    — axial assembly load at top shoulder
  σ_rr free on profile   — thread contact forces (via FEM data)

Loading the FEM solution
------------------------
Use ``SolidMechanicsPipeline.from_fem_solution(solution_npy, spec)``
to add the FEM data as DataConstraint automatically.

functions.name: threaded_coupling_tc50_rotating_default
functions.sig: (body: str = 'BOX', E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, p_inner: float = 20000000.0, F_axial: float = 500000.0, T_torque: float = 40000.0, rpm: float = 90.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
TC50 threaded coupling under combined loading.

Fields  : u_r, u_z, u_θ  (radial, axial, hoop/torsional displacements)
PDE     : axisymmetric linear elasticity (u_r, u_z) + torsion (u_θ)

In linear elasticity the torsion problem decouples from the meridional
problem. The torsional Navier equation is:

    ∂²u_θ/∂r² + (1/r)∂u_θ/∂r − u_θ/r² + ∂²u_θ/∂z² = 0

Torsional stresses (contribute to full Von Mises):

    τ_rθ = μ (∂u_θ/∂r − u_θ/r)
    τ_θz = μ  ∂u_θ/∂z

Full 6-component Von Mises:

    σ_vm = √(½ [(σ_rr−σ_zz)²+(σ_zz−σ_θθ)²+(σ_θθ−σ_rr)²
                + 6(τ_rz²+τ_rθ²+τ_θz²)])

Boundary conditions:
    u_z(r, z=0)  = 0          — fixed nose (thread start)
    u_θ(r, z=0)  = 0          — no rotation at fixed end
    σ_zz(r, z=L) = F/A_cross  — axial traction at top shoulder
    u_θ(r, z=L)  = θ_max · r  — prescribed make-up + rotary twist

Loading
-------
    rpm = 0   → static make-up only (pure torque T_torque)
    rpm > 0   → quasi-static rotation (T_torque includes rotary drag)
    p_inner   → bore pressure (σ_rr = −p at r = r_bore)
    F_axial   → axial tension/compression

functions.sig: (thread_height: float = 0.8, E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, traction_top: float = 100000000.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc: TC50 threaded coupling PIN body — same physics as BOX, different geometry bounds.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.structural
children.doc:
Structural mechanics problem presets.

Covers:
- 2D plane stress / plane strain (linear elasticity)
- Von Mises stress formulation (derives von Mises from displacement fields)
- 3D linear elasticity (brackets, frames)
- Rotary coupling under combined torsion + axial load
- Thermoelasticity 2D/3D

Convention for elasticity:
  E  = Young's modulus (Pa)
  nu = Poisson's ratio
  lambda = E*nu / ((1+nu)*(1-2*nu))  (Lame first)
  mu     = E / (2*(1+nu))             (Lame second / shear modulus)

functions.name: plane_stress_2d_default
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, load_x: float = 0.0, load_y: float = -1000.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D plane stress linear elasticity.

Governing equations (strong form, body force neglected):
    sigma_xx_x + sigma_xy_y = 0
    sigma_xy_x + sigma_yy_y = 0
where sigma = C : eps,  eps = sym(grad u)

Fields: ux (x-displacement), uy (y-displacement)
Derived (post-processing): von Mises stress = sqrt(sigma_xx^2 - sigma_xx*sigma_yy + sigma_yy^2 + 3*sigma_xy^2)

functions.name: plane_strain_2d_default
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc: 2D plane strain linear elasticity (deep structures, dams, tunnels).

functions.name: von_mises_2d_default
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Plane stress with von Mises yield criterion as extra output field.

Fields: ux, uy, vm (von Mises stress, derived).
The PDE is still linear elasticity; vm is a post-processing output
added as an extra field so surrogate models can predict it directly.

functions.name: linear_elasticity_3d
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc: 3D linear elasticity for brackets, frames, and general structures.

functions.name: rotary_coupling_torsion_default
functions.sig: (E: float = 210000000000.0, nu: float = 0.3, r_inner: float = 0.05, r_outer: float = 0.08, torque: float = 10000.0, axial_force: float = 500000.0, length: float = 1.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Rotary coupling under combined torsion and axial tension.

Geometry: hollow cylinder (pipe) of inner radius r_inner, outer radius r_outer,
length `length`. Fixed at z=0, torque T and axial force F applied at z=length.

Fields: ux, uy, uz (displacement components)
Derived: von Mises stress, shear stress, axial stress

Analytical solution (thin-walled):
  tau_max = T * r_outer / J,  J = pi/2 * (r_o^4 - r_i^4)
  sigma_z = F / A,            A = pi * (r_o^2 - r_i^2)
  vm = sqrt(sigma_z^2 + 3*tau^2)

functions.name: thermoelasticity_2d_default
functions.sig: (E: float = 70000000000.0, nu: float = 0.33, alpha_T: float = 2.3e-05, dT: float = 100.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D thermoelastic coupling: thermal expansion due to temperature change.

PDE system:
  - Heat: div(k * grad T) = 0
  - Elasticity: div(sigma) = 0,  sigma = C:(eps - alpha_T * dT * I)

Fields: ux, uy, T

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.tag_geometry
children.doc:
Real-geometry fixtures for ``selector_type="tag"`` presets.

Background
----------
``solve_pde()`` raises ``pinneapple_physics.TagConditionsUnresolved`` for
any ``ProblemSpec`` with ``selector_type="tag"`` conditions unless the
caller supplies real geometry (``x_bc``/``y_bc``/``ctx["tag_masks"]`` plus
a ``mask_<condition_name>`` per tag condition) -- see that exception's
docstring and ``docs/dev/AUDIT_REPORT.md``. Of the 65 registered presets,
40 have at least one ``selector_type="tag"`` condition.

This module is the preset-by-preset engineering judgment call the fix
required: for EACH of those 40, is the preset's own domain a canonical
box/rectangle/cylinder fully described by its own parameters, AND does
each tag name map to one specific face of that shape without guessing at
anything the preset doesn't already state? Only presets that clear BOTH
bars get an entry here. The rest are deliberately left alone --
``TagConditionsUnresolved`` continues to be the correct, honest behavior
for them, because fabricating a plausible-looking box/cylinder for e.g. a
real airfoil or a real furnace refractory geometry would silently produce
physically meaningless (if superficially successful-looking) training
runs, exactly the failure mode this whole fix exists to prevent.

``TAG_GEOMETRY_FIXTURES``: preset name -> a spec dict consumed by
:func:`build_tag_batch`:

    {"shape": "box", "tag_faces": {tag: [(coord, "min"|"max"), ...], ...}}
    {"shape": "cylinder", "axis_coord": ..., "cross_coords": (c0, c1),
     "radius_param": <preset kwarg name, or None to read spec.domain_bounds>,
     "tag_faces": {tag: "inlet"|"outlet"|"wall", ...}}

Every entry below has an inline comment naming the exact text (docstring,
inline comment, or established repo-wide naming convention) the face
mapping is read from -- not invented.

``NOT_FIXABLE_WITHOUT_REAL_GEOMETRY``: the other tag-based presets, each
with a one-line reason (used only for documentation/reporting -- the
actual not-fixable behavior is simply "this module has no entry for it,"
``TagConditionsUnresolved`` still fires).

``CHOSEN_CONVENTIONS`` (added in the 2026-09-17 follow-up pass): a small
number of fixtures below map a tag whose face the preset's own text
genuinely does NOT specify (e.g. "fixed"/"load" on an otherwise-symmetric
unit cube) -- for those, and ONLY those, this pass made an explicit
engineering decision (the canonical cantilever convention, the standard
disc-brake friction/cooling assignment) instead of reading an existing
fact off the preset. Every such fixture is marked in its own inline
comment too; ``CHOSEN_CONVENTIONS`` collects the reasoning in one place so
it can never be mistaken for the preset's own text the way every other
entry's comment is.

functions.doc:
Build a real-geometry batch for preset ``name`` using its
:data:`TAG_GEOMETRY_FIXTURES` entry. Raises ``KeyError`` if ``name``
has no fixture (i.e. it is one of the ``NOT_FIXABLE_WITHOUT_REAL_
GEOMETRY`` presets, or an untagged preset that needs no fixture at all).

functions.sig: (name: str, spec: ProblemSpec, *, n_bc_per_face: int = 1000, seed: int = 7) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
The extra ``solve_pde`` keyword arguments preset ``name`` needs: ``{}`` when ``spec`` has no
``selector_type="tag"`` condition, the :func:`build_tag_batch` geometry when it has a fixture here, and
``KeyError`` otherwise (the honest failure: no geometry is invented)::

    pp.solve_pde(spec, model, epochs=..., **tag_solve_kwargs(name, spec))

Strip the ``x_col`` key (``solve_pde`` samples its own collocation
points from ``spec.domain_bounds`` and doesn't accept one) and convert
numpy arrays to torch tensors, ready to splat into
``solve_pde(spec, model, **solve_pde_kwargs_from_batch(batch))``.

functions.doc:
Every loss term of ``compile_problem(spec)`` for ``model`` on a :func:`build_tag_batch` batch, as floats:
``total``, ``pde`` and one entry per boundary condition (``bc_<name>``), so the per-tag masking can be seen to
do distinct work. Numpy arrays of the batch are converted to torch tensors (``mask_*`` as booleans).

:func:`~pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.registry.get_preset` writes, or ``""``.

functions.doc: True when this spec's tag conditions can be satisfied by its own fixture.

functions.sig: (spec: ProblemSpec, *, n_bc_per_face: int = 1000, seed: int = 7) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
The ``solve_pde`` keyword arguments that satisfy this spec's tag conditions with the preset's
own box or cylinder geometry, or ``{}`` when the spec has no fixture.

This is the difference between ``pp.solve("pipe_flow_3d", method="pinn")`` working out of the box
and raising ``TagConditionsUnresolved``: the geometry is the one the preset already declares
(see :data:`TAG_GEOMETRY_FIXTURES`), nothing is invented here.

>>> import pinneapple as pp
>>> from pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.tag_geometry import default_geometry
>>> kw = default_geometry(pp.get_preset("poisson_2d"))     # {'x_bc': ..., 'ctx': {...}, ...}
>>> sorted(kw)[:2]

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.terramechanics
children.doc:
Terramechanics physics residuals and preset for Bekker-Wong PINN surrogate.

Usage
-----
from pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.terramechanics import (
    TerramechanicsResiduals,
    bekker_wong_surrogate_2d,
)

residuals = TerramechanicsResiduals()
r_dict = residuals(model, norm_x, norm_y)
loss = sum(v.mean() for v in r_dict.values())

classes.name: TerramechanicsResiduals
classes.sig: (c_Pa: float = 1400.0, phi_deg: float = 30.0, R_m: float = 0.125, b_m: float = 0.06, n_phys: int = 256, R_factor: float = 0.06, slip_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.75), sink_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.002, 0.058))
classes.doc:
Physics residuals for the Bekker-Wong PINN surrogate.

Only constraints that were checked numerically against the Bekker-Wong solver
(``pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.bekker_wong``) on the preset domain
s in [0, 0.75], z in [0.002, 0.058] m (GRC-1 defaults) are imposed:

R2 -- Mohr-Coulomb traction limit: F_x <= c*A + F_z*tan(phi), A = b*R*theta_1   (ReLU^2)
R3 -- Pre-peak monotonicity: dF_x/ds >= 0 for s in [0, 0.4]                      (autograd)
R4 -- Torque coupling: M_y >= R * F_x
R5 -- Load monotonicity: dF_z/dz >= 0

Removed: the former "R1: F_x(s=0) = 0". It is not a property of the Bekker-Wong model:
at zero slip the shear displacement j(theta) = R[(theta_f-theta) - (sin theta_f - sin theta)]
is non-zero, and the solver returns F_x(0, z) between about -4.2 N and +5.0 N on the
preset domain (compaction resistance vs. rear-region shear). Imposing it biased the
surrogate against its own training data. R3 is only valid on the domain above -- it is
violated for sinkages beyond ~0.06 m, so re-check it before widening the domain.

Parameters
----------
c_Pa : soil cohesion [Pa]
phi_deg : internal friction angle [degrees]
R_m : wheel radius [m]
b_m : wheel width [m]
n_phys : number of collocation points per residual
R_factor : scale factor converting normalised M_y vs F_x for R4
slip_range, sink_range : collocation domain (must stay inside the verified domain)

functions.name: bekker_wong_surrogate_2d
functions.sig: (c_Pa: float = 1400.0, phi_deg: float = 30.0, R_m: float = 0.125, b_m: float = 0.06) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
Return a ProblemSpec for the 2-D Bekker-Wong PINN surrogate.

Inputs : (slip_ratio, sinkage_m)
Outputs: (F_x, F_z, M_y)

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.presets.turbomachinery
children.doc:
Turbomachinery problem presets.

Covers axial compressor physics for use with TurboDesigner as a data/constraint source:
  - axial_compressor_meanline   : 1D mean-line (Euler work + continuity + energy)
  - axial_compressor_cascade_2d : 2D blade-to-blade cascade (compressible Euler)
  - axial_compressor_stage_3d   : 3D single-stage in cylindrical coords (rotating Euler)

The ``solver_spec["name"] = "turbodesigner"`` signals that
``pinneapple_simulation.external_solvers.turbodesigner`` can generate training
data for these problems from analytical mean-line solutions.

functions.name: axial_compressor_meanline
functions.sig: (num_stages: int = 5, pressure_ratio: float = 3.0, mass_flow_rate: float = 4.37, rpm: float = 10000.0, inlet_total_pressure: float = 101325.0, inlet_total_temperature: float = 288.15, isentropic_efficiency: float = 0.878, hub_to_tip_ratio: float = 0.5, axial_velocity: float = 136.0, gamma: float = 1.4, R_gas: float = 287.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
1D mean-line thermodynamic analysis of a multi-stage axial compressor.

Solves Euler work equation, continuity, and isentropic relations along
the streamwise coordinate s ∈ [0, 1] (inlet to outlet, normalised).

PDE residuals (stage-averaged, kind="compressor_meanline_1d"):
  - Energy    : c_p * d(T_t)/ds = W_stage / L_machine
  - Continuity: d(rho * u * A)/ds = 0
  - State     : p_t = rho * R_gas * T_t  (ideal gas)

Fields  : T_t (K), p_t (Pa), rho (kg/m³), u (m/s), c_theta (m/s)
Coords  : s  (dimensionless streamwise, 0 = inlet, 1 = outlet)

Parameters
----------
num_stages              : number of compressor stages
pressure_ratio          : overall total pressure ratio (p_tout / p_tin)
mass_flow_rate          : kg/s
rpm                     : shaft speed in rev/min
inlet_total_pressure    : Pa
inlet_total_temperature : K
isentropic_efficiency   : stage polytropic efficiency (0–1)
hub_to_tip_ratio        : h/t ratio at inlet
axial_velocity          : mean axial velocity (m/s), used as inlet BC
gamma                   : specific heat ratio
R_gas                   : gas constant J/(kg·K)

functions.name: axial_compressor_cascade_2d
functions.sig: (inlet_mach: float = 0.5, flow_angle_in_deg: float = 50.0, flow_angle_out_deg: float = 20.0, chord: float = 0.1, pitch_to_chord: float = 0.8, gamma: float = 1.4, R_gas: float = 287.0, p_inlet: float = 101325.0, T_inlet: float = 288.15) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
2D compressible Euler flow through an axial compressor blade cascade.

Models the blade-to-blade passage between adjacent blades.  The domain is
a 2D channel (x = axial, y = pitch) with periodic BC in y implied by the
blade row symmetry.

PDE: steady 2D compressible Euler (kind="compressible_euler_2d").
Fields : rho, u (axial), v (tangential), p, T
Coords : (x, y)

Parameters
----------
inlet_mach        : inlet absolute Mach number
flow_angle_in_deg : inlet flow angle from axial (deg), positive = swirl
flow_angle_out_deg: design outlet flow angle from axial (deg)
chord             : blade chord length (m)
pitch_to_chord    : blade pitch / chord
gamma, R_gas      : thermodynamic constants
p_inlet, T_inlet  : inlet total conditions (Pa, K)

functions.name: axial_compressor_stage_3d
functions.sig: (rpm: float = 10000.0, pressure_ratio_stage: float = 1.4, mass_flow_rate: float = 4.37, hub_radius: float = 0.1, tip_radius: float = 0.2, axial_length: float = 0.15, inlet_total_pressure: float = 101325.0, inlet_total_temperature: float = 288.15, isentropic_efficiency: float = 0.88, gamma: float = 1.4, R_gas: float = 287.0) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
3D single compressor stage in cylindrical coordinates (r, theta, z).

Models the rotor passage using steady 3D compressible Euler equations in
a rotating reference frame (rotating at ``rpm``).  The PINN learns the
full 3D flow field including spanwise redistribution and tip effects.

PDE: steady 3D compressible Euler, rotating frame (kind="compressible_euler_rotating_3d").
Fields : rho, u_r, u_theta, u_z, p, T
Coords : (r, theta, z)

Parameters
----------
rpm                     : rotor speed (rev/min)
pressure_ratio_stage    : stage total-to-total pressure ratio
mass_flow_rate          : kg/s
hub_radius              : hub radius at rotor inlet (m)
tip_radius              : tip radius at rotor inlet (m)
axial_length            : rotor axial chord (m)
inlet_total_pressure    : Pa
inlet_total_temperature : K
isentropic_efficiency   : stage isentropic efficiency (0–1)
gamma, R_gas            : thermodynamic constants

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.reconcile
children.doc:
Reconciling the three problem specifications: decision D1 of the strategy (issue #150).

PINNeAPPle grew three descriptions of "a problem", each correct where it is used and none of them a superset:

============================  ===========================================================================
``pinneapple_problemdesign``  the **elicited** description: what the user *said*, still free text -- a goal,
``.schema.ProblemSpec``       equations as strings, geometry as a sentence, constraints and risks. Nothing in it
                              is compilable, on purpose: it is what a conversation produces before anybody decides
                              which equations are meant.
``pinneapple_physics``        the **PDE** description: coordinates, fields, the ``PDETermSpec`` the compiler and the
``.pde_environment.spec``     solvers switch on, conditions with selectors and value functions, bounds and a
``.ProblemSpec``              reference solver. This is the one that runs.
``pinneapple_data``           the **sampling** description: one condition of a UPD shard -- a ``type`` (initial /
``.upd_types.ConditionSpec``  boundary / interior / slice), the equation string kept for coordination, ``n`` points
                              and free-form options. It says how many points, not what the physics is.
============================  ===========================================================================

Conversion has to exist because a project starts elicited, is solved as a PDE and is stored as samples; and the
conversion has to be **explicit** because two of the three are lossy in one direction each, and a converter that
hides that is how a wrong problem reaches a solver.

The pivot is :class:`pinneapple_physics.physical_problem.PhysicalProblem`, which already carries tested adapters to
both ``ProblemSpec`` flavours (``from_problem_design`` / ``to_problem_design``, ``from_pde_spec`` / ``to_pde_spec``).
The functions here are the direct, named conversions on top of those, with the loss written down in
:data:`LOSSES` rather than discovered later, plus the condition-level bridge between the sampling and the PDE
description, which did not exist at all.

Nothing here adds a class: D1 says the three specifications stay as they are, and this module is functions over
them. The record of the decision, with the field-by-field table, is ``docs/strategy/D1_problem_specs.md``.

>>> import pinneapple as pp
>>> from pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.reconcile import pde_to_design, design_to_pde
>>> spec = pp.PhysicalProblem.from_preset("burgers_1d").to_pde_spec()
>>> design = pde_to_design(spec)                       # what a report or the assistant shows
>>> back = design_to_pde(design)                       # and back to something a solver can take
>>> back.fields, back.coords, back.domain_bounds

classes.name: ConditionBridge
classes.doc: A converted condition, the data the target cannot hold, and what the conversion could not do.

functions.name: pde_to_design
functions.sig: (spec: ProblemSpec)
functions.doc:
The elicited description of a PDE ``ProblemSpec`` (for reports, the assistant and the plan text).

Goes through ``PhysicalProblem``, which owns the tested mapping and the task vocabulary; see
:data:`LOSSES` for what an elicited description cannot hold.

functions.name: design_to_pde
functions.sig: (design: Any, *, pde_kind: str, coords: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, fields: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, domain_bounds: Optional[Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]] = None) -> ProblemSpec
functions.doc:
A PDE ``ProblemSpec`` from an elicited one.

``pde_kind`` is required and has no default on purpose: the elicited description says "heat conduction in a
fin" in prose, and which ``pde.kind`` the solvers switch on is a decision somebody makes, not something the
converter may guess. ``coords``, ``fields`` and ``domain_bounds`` fill what the text left implicit; whatever
the elicited side carries and the PDE side cannot hold (goal, risks, data plan, assumptions) goes to
``spec.meta['elicited']`` rather than being dropped.

functions.name: upd_condition_to_pde
functions.sig: (cond: Any, *, fields: Sequence[str], value: Optional[float] = None) -> ConditionBridge
functions.doc:
A PDE ``ConditionSpec`` from a sampling ``pinneapple_data.upd_types.ConditionSpec``.

``fields`` are the fields the condition applies to (the sampling side has no idea, it stores climate variables).
The equation string and the point count travel in ``carried``: a PDE condition is written as a selector and a
value function, and inventing one from a string would be a guess. ``value`` attaches a constant value function,
which is the only value the sampling side can express.

functions.name: pde_condition_to_upd
functions.sig: (cond: ConditionSpec, *, carried: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, n: Optional[int] = None) -> Any
functions.doc:
A sampling ``ConditionSpec`` from a PDE one: the shared fields, plus what ``carried`` hands back.

A PDE condition with a Python value function has no equation string of its own; passing the ``carried`` dict
from :func:`upd_condition_to_pde` makes the round trip lossless for everything the sampling side can hold.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.turbulence_presets
children.doc:
RANS/LES turbulence closure presets for PINN training.

Implements k-omega SST (Menter 1994) and Spalart-Allmaras (SA, 1992) RANS
models (2D, steady), and WALE (Nicoud & Ducros, 1999) as an algebraic,
genuinely 3D, transient LES closure, as PDE residual functions compatible
with PINNeAPPle's PINNFactory.

Each residual class is callable:
    residuals = KOmegaSSTResiduals(nu=1e-5, rho=1.0)
    r_dict = residuals(model, x_col)   # returns dict of residual tensors

The dict keys match the equation names and can be directly summed into a
PINN loss::

    loss = sum(r.pow(2).mean() for r in r_dict.values())

classes.name: KOmegaSSTResiduals
classes.sig: (nu: float = 1e-05, rho: float = 1.0, consts: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> None
classes.doc:
k-omega SST two-equation turbulence model residuals for PINN.

Equations solved (steady RANS, incompressible mean flow):

2D form -- ``model: (N,2) -> (N,5)``, ``(x,y) -> (u,v,p,k,omega)``::

    Momentum-x:  rho*(u u_x + v u_y) + p_x - d/dx[(mu+mu_t) 2 u_x]
                 - d/dy[(mu+mu_t)(u_y + v_x)] = 0
    Momentum-y:  rho*(u v_x + v v_y) + p_y - d/dx[(mu+mu_t)(u_y + v_x)]
                 - d/dy[(mu+mu_t) 2 v_y] = 0
    Continuity:  u_x + v_y = 0
    k-equation:  u k_x + v k_y - d/dx[(nu+sigma_k nu_t) k_x]
                 - d/dy[(nu+sigma_k nu_t) k_y] - P_k + beta* k omega = 0
    omega-eq:    u w_x + v w_y - d/dx[(nu+sigma_w nu_t) w_x]
                 - d/dy[(nu+sigma_w nu_t) w_y]
                 - gamma P_k/nu_t + beta omega^2 - CD_kw = 0

3D form -- ``model: (N,3) -> (N,6)``, ``(x,y,z) -> (u,v,w,p,k,omega)``,
the genuine 3D generalization of the above (mirroring how
``WALEResiduals`` below went from a 2D-style helper to a real 3D LES
closure): every equation gains the third velocity component and its
z-derivatives, and the viscous/diffusion terms gain the full set of
z-direction cross terms (no incompressibility-based term-dropping --
mu_eff/nu_eff still vary spatially, exactly as in the 2D case)::

    Momentum-i (i=x,y,z):  rho*(u.grad)u_i + p_i
                 - div[(mu+mu_t)*(grad u_i + grad u^T e_i)] = 0
    Continuity:  u_x + v_y + w_z = 0
    k-equation:  u k_x + v k_y + w k_z - div[(nu+sigma_k nu_t) grad k]
                 - P_k + beta_star*k*omega = 0
    omega-eq:    u w_x + v w_y + w w_z - div[(nu+sigma_w nu_t) grad omega]
                 - gamma*S_mag^2 + beta*omega^2 - CD_kw = 0

where ``S_mag = sqrt(2 S_ij S_ij)`` now uses the full 3D symmetric
strain-rate tensor (6 independent components: S_11=u_x, S_22=v_y,
S_33=w_z, S_12=0.5(u_y+v_x), S_13=0.5(u_z+w_x), S_23=0.5(v_z+w_y))
and ``CD_kw`` uses the 3D cross-diffusion ``k_x w_x + k_y w_y + k_z w_z``.

``__call__`` dispatches on ``x_col.shape[1]`` (2 -> :meth:`_call_2d`,
the original, numerically-unchanged 2D path; 3 -> :meth:`_call_3d`,
the new 3D path below) so existing 2D callers keep their exact
residual values. ``self.eddy_viscosity``, ``self._blend_const`` and
``SST_CONSTS`` are reused unchanged by both paths -- the constants and
blending-function machinery are dimension-independent. The unrelated
1D :meth:`channel_residuals` reduction (used by
``templates/33_rans_turbulence.py``) is untouched by any of this.

Usage::

    residuals = KOmegaSSTResiduals(nu=1e-5, rho=1.0)
    r = residuals(model_uvpkw, x_col)      # x_col: (N,2) -> 2D path
    r3 = residuals(model_uvwpkw, x_col3d)  # x_col3d: (N,3) -> 3D path
    # r is a dict with keys: momentum_x, momentum_y, [momentum_z,]
    #                        continuity, k_eq, omega_eq
    loss = sum(v.pow(2).mean() for v in r.values())

methods.name: eddy_viscosity
methods.sig: (k: torch.Tensor, omega: torch.Tensor, S_mag: torch.Tensor, F2: float = 1.0) -> torch.Tensor
methods.doc: Compute turbulent viscosity mu_t (Bradshaw limiter included).

methods.name: channel_residuals
methods.sig: (y: torch.Tensor, U: torch.Tensor, k: torch.Tensor, omega: torch.Tensor, u_tau: float = 1.0, delta: float = 1.0, F2: float = 1.0) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
methods.doc:
1D (wall-normal-only) k-omega SST reduction for fully-developed
plane channel flow -- every streamwise derivative is zero by the
fully-developed assumption, and the mean-momentum equation reduces
to a total-shear-stress balance driven by the constant wall-unit
pressure gradient ``-u_tau**2/delta`` (see e.g. Pope, *Turbulent
Flows*, Ch. 7, for the derivation). This is the convenience form a
1D channel-flow PINN wants; :meth:`__call__` is the general 2D
form.

classes.name: SpalartAllmarasResiduals
classes.sig: (nu: float = 1e-05) -> None
classes.doc:
Spalart-Allmaras one-equation turbulence model residuals.

Transport equation for modified eddy viscosity nu_tilde::

    D nu_tilde / Dt = cb1 * S_tilde * nu_tilde
                    - cw1 * fw * (nu_tilde / d)^2
                    + (1/sigma) * div[(nu + nu_tilde) grad nu_tilde]
                    + (cb2/sigma) |grad nu_tilde|^2

Usage::

    sa = SpalartAllmarasResiduals(nu=1e-5)
    r = sa(model_uvpn, x_col, wall_distance_fn=lambda x: x[:,1:2])
    # r: dict with 'momentum_x', 'momentum_y', 'continuity', 'sa_eq'

classes.name: WALEResiduals
classes.sig: (nu: float = 1e-05, cw: float = 0.325, delta = 1.0, spatial_indices = (0, 1, 2), t_index: int = 3) -> None
classes.doc:
WALE (Wall-Adapting Local Eddy-viscosity) subgrid closure for
filtered incompressible Navier-Stokes -- Nicoud & Ducros (1999) -- as
an algebraic (no transport equation) 3D LES residual.

Unlike the RANS closures above, WALE needs no extra transported
unknowns: the eddy viscosity is a pointwise algebraic function of the
resolved velocity-gradient tensor, so the model only maps
``(x, y, z, t) -> (u, v, w, p)`` -- and, unlike the 2D-only RANS
closures in this module, the residual itself is a genuine 3D one (the
only LES/3D-turbulence closure in this module as of this addition;
everything else here is 2D steady RANS).

::

    nu_sgs = (Cw*Delta)^2 * (Sd:Sd)^{3/2} / ((S:S)^{5/2} + (Sd:Sd)^{5/4})

where ``S`` is the resolved strain-rate tensor and ``Sd`` is the
traceless symmetric part of the squared velocity-gradient tensor.
``Delta`` is the LES filter width; pass either a constant (uniform
mesh) or a callable ``delta_fn(x) -> (N, 1)`` (e.g. a mesh-derived
``cubeRootVol`` lookup -- see ``pinneapple_simulation.external_solvers
.openfoam.mesh_reader`` for the per-cell sizes such a lookup would be
built from).

Usage::

    residuals = WALEResiduals(nu=1e-5, cw=0.325, delta=0.01)
    r = residuals(model_uvwp, x_col)   # x_col: (N, 4) = (x, y, z, t)
    loss = sum(v.pow(2).mean() for k, v in r.items() if k != "nu_sgs")

A spatially-uniform, time-independent driving source (matching
OpenFOAM's ``meanVelocityForce`` fvOption for a periodic channel/duct
held to a target bulk velocity) can be folded in via the optional
``forcing`` argument to ``__call__`` -- e.g. a
``torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(3))`` learned jointly with the
network and pinned down by an auxiliary bulk-velocity penalty in the
training loop (that penalty is problem data, not part of this
closure, so it is not computed here).

functions.name: get_rans_preset
functions.sig: (model_name: str = 'k-omega-sst', **kwargs)
functions.doc:
Get a RANS/LES turbulence closure residual object by name.

Parameters
----------
model_name : one of 'k-omega-sst', 'spalart-allmaras', 'sa', 'wale'
**kwargs   : forwarded to the residual class constructor

Returns
-------
Callable residual object (KOmegaSSTResiduals, SpalartAllmarasResiduals
or WALEResiduals)

Examples
--------
>>> res = get_rans_preset("k-omega-sst", nu=1e-5, rho=1.0)
>>> res = get_rans_preset("spalart-allmaras", nu=1.5e-5)
>>> res = get_rans_preset("wale", nu=1e-5, cw=0.325, delta=0.01)

children.summary: RANS/LES turbulence closure presets for PINN training.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.turbulence_selector
children.doc:
Unified turbulence-model selector.

Real turbulence closures already exist in this repo in three disjoint
places:

  * ``pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.turbulence_presets`` --
    ``KOmegaSSTResiduals`` (RANS, PINN-residual style, dispatches on
    ``x_col.shape[1]`` to give a 2D or 3D closure at *call* time) and
    ``WALEResiduals`` (LES, PINN-residual style, genuinely 3D only).
  * ``pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.lbm`` -- Smagorinsky LES via
    the scalar ``Cs`` parameter accepted by ``LBMSolver``/``LBMSolver3D``
    (LBM-native: not a PINN residual object at all, just a number).

This module is pure dispatch/validation glue over those two families -- it
constructs and returns the real objects (or the real ``Cs`` parameter) and
does not reimplement any turbulence physics itself.

classes.name: TurbulenceModel
classes.doc:
Turbulence closure selector.

``LAMINAR``          -- no turbulence closure.
``RANS_K_OMEGA_SST``  -- Menter (1994) k-omega SST, PINN-residual style
                         (:class:`KOmegaSSTResiduals`).
``LES_WALE``          -- Nicoud & Ducros (1999) WALE, PINN-residual
                         style, genuinely 3D only (:class:`WALEResiduals`).
``LES_SMAGORINSKY``   -- Smagorinsky LES, LBM-native (a scalar ``Cs``
                         constant, not a PINN residual object).

functions.name: get_turbulence_closure
functions.sig: (model: TurbulenceModel | str, dim: int = 3, solver_family: str = 'pinn', **kwargs) -> Any | None
functions.doc:
Return the right turbulence closure object/parameter for a solver family.

This function only dispatches to and validates against the *existing*
closures -- it never computes turbulence physics itself.

Parameters
----------
model : TurbulenceModel | str
    One of ``TurbulenceModel``'s members (or the equivalent string
    value, e.g. ``"les_wale"``).
dim : int
    Spatial dimension, 2 or 3. For ``solver_family="pinn"``:

    * ``RANS_K_OMEGA_SST`` -- :class:`KOmegaSSTResiduals` itself
      dispatches 2D vs. 3D at *call* time from the collocation points'
      shape (``x_col.shape[1]``), not at construction time, so ``dim``
      is only used here to validate it is 2 or 3 (it is not forwarded
      to the constructor, which has no ``dim`` parameter).
    * ``LES_WALE`` -- :class:`WALEResiduals` is a genuinely-3D-only
      closure (see its docstring); ``dim=2`` raises ``ValueError``.

    Ignored for ``solver_family="lbm"`` (the in-repo LBM solvers'
    Smagorinsky support is dimension-agnostic: the same scalar ``Cs``
    is accepted by both ``LBMSolver`` (D2Q9) and ``LBMSolver3D`` (D3Q19)).
solver_family : {"pinn", "lbm"}
    Which closure family to dispatch into.
**kwargs
    Forwarded to the underlying closure's constructor
    (``solver_family="pinn"``) or used to look up ``Cs``
    (``solver_family="lbm"``, ``model=LES_SMAGORINSKY``).

Returns
-------
* ``solver_family="pinn"``: ``None`` (LAMINAR), a configured
  :class:`KOmegaSSTResiduals` (RANS_K_OMEGA_SST), or a configured
  :class:`WALEResiduals` (LES_WALE).
* ``solver_family="lbm"``: ``0.0`` (LAMINAR, i.e. ``Cs=0`` / pure BGK)
  or a ``float`` Smagorinsky constant ``Cs`` (LES_SMAGORINSKY).

Raises
------
ValueError
    For any model/solver_family combination that has no implementation
    in this repo (e.g. LES_SMAGORINSKY under "pinn", or
    RANS_K_OMEGA_SST/LES_WALE under "lbm"), or for an unrecognized
    ``model``/``solver_family``/``dim``.

children.summary: Unified turbulence-model selector.
Problem specification: PDE terms, conditions, scales, presets, turbulence models and PDE families.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.physical_problem
children.doc:
``PhysicalProblem``: one description of a physics problem for every part of the library.

Before this module there were three overlapping classes, each covering part of a problem:

* ``pinneapple_physics.pde_environment.spec.ProblemSpec`` -- the executable PDE definition (coordinates,
  fields, PDE term, boundary/initial/data conditions, domain bounds). The PINN compiler consumes it.
* ``pinneapple_problemdesign.schema.ProblemSpec`` -- the elicited, mostly free-text description of a problem
  (goal, task type, data, validation and deployment needs) produced by the problem-design assistant.
* ``pinneapple_data.physics_case.PhysicsCase`` -- a bundle that references geometry, a PDE ``ProblemSpec``,
  a solver choice, results and a reference benchmark.

``PhysicalProblem`` holds all of that in one place and adds what none of them had: **parameters with units
and a role** (fixed, design, uncertain, unknown), so the same object can drive a forward solve, a design
optimization, an uncertainty study or a parameter-discovery run, plus **quantities of interest** and a
stable **fingerprint** for provenance.

The three existing classes keep working unchanged. They are adapters:

>>> import pinneapple as pp
>>> prob = pp.PhysicalProblem.from_preset("burgers_1d", nu=0.01)
>>> spec = prob.to_pde_spec()                 # what the PINN compiler consumes, same object shape as before
>>> pp.PhysicalProblem.from_pde_spec(spec).to_pde_spec() == spec
True

Units are optional but checked when given (``pinneapple_data.physical_units``); ``validate()`` reports
inconsistencies (unknown fields in a condition, a value outside its bounds, an unparseable unit) as a list
of readable strings instead of failing later inside a solver.

classes.name: Parameter
classes.doc:
A named physical parameter.

role:
  * ``fixed``     -- known value, held constant (the default).
  * ``design``    -- a design variable an optimizer may move within ``bounds``.
  * ``uncertain`` -- known only as a distribution (``distribution``) or interval (``bounds``); used by UQ.
  * ``unknown``   -- to be identified from data (parameter discovery); ``value`` is the initial guess.

``unit`` is a unit string such as ``"m^2/s"`` or ``"Pa"`` (``None`` means not stated, ``"1"`` means
dimensionless). ``distribution`` is a plain dict, e.g. ``{"type": "normal", "mean": 0.01, "std": 0.001}``.

classes.name: Quantity
classes.doc:
A quantity of interest: what the user actually wants out of the solution (a field, a coefficient,
a peak value). ``field`` names the model output it derives from, when there is one.

classes.name: Objective
classes.doc:
What the problem is *for*: a quantity to minimise, maximise, or drive to a target (issue #151).

``quantity`` names a ``Quantity`` (or a field) of the same problem; ``target`` is required when ``sense`` is
``"target"`` and ignored otherwise. ``weight`` lets several objectives be combined without losing which one
mattered more, and ``unit`` is the unit of ``target``/``tolerance``.

classes.name: Constraint
classes.doc:
A limit the answer has to satisfy: a bound on a quantity, or an expression over parameters (#151, #221).

``kind="bound"`` uses ``quantity``/``op``/``value``; ``kind="expression"`` uses ``expression`` (free text, the
same form the elicited description and the design-of-experiments ``ParameterSpace`` already accept).

``family`` says **what kind of limit** it is -- ``"physical"`` (a physical limit: a temperature or a yield
stress), ``"conservation"`` (a conserved total), ``"operational"`` (a derating or an operating envelope),
``"material"``, ``"actuator"`` (a stroke or a rate) or ``"safety"`` -- and ``""`` leaves it unlabelled for the
constraints that predate the vocabulary. The family does not change how the limit is *checked*: that is the
point of #221, one object and one arithmetic applied in training, in an optimizer and in a deployment guard
(:mod:`pinneapple_physics.constraint_engine`). It is the label the report groups by, the optimizer names its
constraint with, and the guard puts in its refusal.

``weight`` scales the penalty the constraint contributes during training, and ``hard`` says whether a violation
is fatal: a hard constraint stops a deployment and rejects a design, a soft one is reported and penalised but
lets the answer through.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The constraint as one line, for the elicited description and for a report.

classes.name: Fidelity
classes.doc:
How much physics the answer has to have, and how good it has to be (#151).

``level`` is the physics: ``"closed_form"``, ``"linear"``, ``"rans"``, ``"les"``, ``"dns"``, ``"surrogate"`` or
``"unspecified"``. ``mesh_level`` names a mesh (``"L1"``, ``"coarse"``) when the answer depends on one, and
``tolerance`` is the relative error the result has to meet against its reference.

classes.name: PhysicalProblem
classes.doc:
A complete physics problem: geometry, physics, conditions, parameters, solver choice and intent.

Only ``name`` is required. A problem can be described before its geometry exists, before the PDE is
known (for example right after the problem-design conversation) or before it has been solved.

Attributes
----------
coords, fields : coordinate and output-field names, e.g. ``("x", "t")`` and ``("u",)``.
pde : the governing equation as a ``PDETermSpec`` (``kind`` + ``params``), or ``None``.
conditions : boundary, initial, interface and data constraints (``ConditionSpec``).
domain_bounds : axis-aligned bounds per coordinate, e.g. ``{"x": (-1, 1), "t": (0, 1)}``.
geometry : a geometry object (mesh, CAD, voxel grid, SDF...) when the domain is not a box.
parameters : ``Parameter`` objects keyed by name. ``pde.params`` values are kept in sync on export.
units : unit per coordinate or field name, e.g. ``{"x": "m", "u": "m/s"}``.
quantities : quantities of interest.
solver, solver_config : the solver/backend chosen for this problem and its options.
reference_solver : how reference solutions for this problem are produced (a preset's ``solver_spec``).
task : what is being asked: ``"forward"``, ``"inverse"``, ``"design"``, ``"uq"``, ``"surrogate"`` or free text.
objectives : ``Objective`` objects -- what the answer is for (minimise drag, hold peak temperature under X).
constraints : ``Constraint`` objects -- the limits the answer has to satisfy, as bounds or expressions.
fidelity : how much physics and how good the answer has to be (``Fidelity``), or ``None``.
geometry_ref : a path or URI to the CAD/mesh the domain came from, when there is one.
intent : free-text context (goal, data, validation, deployment) carried over from problem design.
references, metadata : citations and free-form provenance.

methods.name: parameter_values
methods.doc: Current value of every parameter that has one (what the PDE residual needs).

methods.name: with_parameters
methods.doc: A copy with new parameter values (unknown names raise, so typos do not pass silently).

methods.name: set_role
methods.sig: (name: str, role: str, *, bounds: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None, distribution: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> 'PhysicalProblem'
methods.doc: A copy where parameter ``name`` has a new role, e.g. ``set_role("nu", "unknown")`` for discovery.

methods.name: backend
methods.doc: The trainer for this problem on ``backend``: ``"pytorch"``, ``"jax"`` or ``"physicsnemo"``.

methods.name: unit_names

children.name: pinneapple_physics.physics_audit
pinneapple_physics.physics_audit.assumptions
children.doc:
Physics assumptions of a model, the conditions under which each holds, and an auditor that checks them case by
case.

Every surrogate, PINN or solver rests on simplifications: incompressible flow, laminar regime, constant properties,
small strains. Each holds inside a range of dimensionless numbers. A model used outside that range can still return
a smooth, plausible field, and its PDE residual can even stay low (it satisfies *its* equations, which no longer
describe the case). So the first place to look for the cause of an error is the model's own physical foundations.

* :class:`Condition`: ``lo <= feature <= hi``, with a soft band around the edges (in decades for numbers that span
  orders of magnitude) so the auditor says *marginal* near a transition instead of flipping from valid to violated;
* :class:`Assumption`: a named simplification, its conditions, the phenomenon that appears when it breaks and the
  physical mechanism the model then lacks. :data:`ASSUMPTIONS` holds the common ones; the factory functions
  (:func:`laminar`, :func:`incompressible`...) build them with other thresholds;
* :class:`Envelope`: where the model was trained (box of feature ranges, optionally the training samples for a
  nearest-neighbour distance), for extrapolation;
* :class:`ModelProfile`: the model card the audit reads: equations, assumptions, mechanisms represented, envelope;
* :func:`audit_assumptions` / :class:`AssumptionAudit`: one case against one profile, with a status per assumption
  (``VALID``, ``MARGINAL``, ``VIOLATED``, ``UNKNOWN`` when the feature is missing: never a silent pass), a
  compatibility score in [0, 1] and the phenomena the case probably triggers.

classes.name: Condition
classes.doc:
``lo <= features[feature] <= hi``. ``band``: width of the soft edge, in decades when ``log`` (default for
positive bounds), in feature units otherwise. Inside but within ``band`` of an edge is marginal; outside by more
than ``band`` is violated. :meth:`score` is 1 inside and decays as exp(-(d / band)^2) outside.

methods.name: distance
methods.doc: Signed distance to the nearest edge: negative inside, positive outside (decades when log).

classes.name: Assumption
classes.doc:
A simplification a model rests on. ``breaks_into``: the phenomenon that appears when it fails (turbulence,
compressibility...); ``missing_mechanism``: what the model then lacks (turbulent transport, density
variation...).

classes.name: Envelope
classes.doc:
Where a model was trained or validated. ``ranges``: {feature: (lo, hi)}; ``samples``: optional
(n, d) training points over ``sample_features`` for a nearest-neighbour distance (in units of the median
neighbour spacing of the training set, on standardised features, log10 for positive features).

methods.name: from_samples
methods.sig: (samples: Sequence[Mapping[str, float]], features: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> Envelope

methods.name: check
methods.doc: ``inside`` (all ranges), ``score`` in [0, 1], per-feature lines and, with samples, ``knn_distance``.

classes.name: ModelProfile
classes.doc:
What the audit knows about a model: family (``"PINN"``, ``"FNO"``, ``"solver"``...), governing equations,
assumptions (names from :data:`ASSUMPTIONS` or :class:`Assumption` objects), mechanisms it represents
(``"turbulent transport"``...), training envelope and relative cost.

functions.name: laminar
functions.sig: (re_crit: float = 2300.0, feature: str = 'Re', geometry: str = 'pipe') -> Assumption
functions.doc: Laminar flow below the transition Reynolds number (2300 in a pipe; about 5e5 on a flat plate, by x).

functions.name: turbulent
functions.sig: (re_min: float = 4000.0, re_max: float = math.inf, feature: str = 'Re') -> Assumption
functions.doc:
Fully turbulent flow (wall functions, turbulent correlations such as Blasius or Colebrook). The phenomenon
named is the one below ``re_min``; state an upper limit of a correlation through the training envelope or a
separate assumption (:func:`hydraulically_smooth`).

functions.name: hydraulically_smooth

functions.doc:
Smooth wall: roughness buried in the viscous sublayer, roughness Reynolds number eps+ = Re (eps / D)
sqrt(f / 8) below about 5 (see :func:`~.regime.roughness_reynolds`).

children.summary: Physics assumptions of a model, the conditions under which each holds, and an auditor that checks them case by case.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.physics_audit.attribution
children.doc:
Physics failure attribution: not only *that* a prediction is wrong (or suspect), but its probable cause, with the
evidence and a confidence.

The causes, and the evidence each one rests on:

=========================  ==============================================================================
``pde_violation``          the governing-equation residual fails its tolerance or jumps above its baseline
``conservation``           a conserved total (mass, energy, momentum) is off
``boundary_condition``     the prediction does not meet the boundary condition
``regime_change``          the case violates an assumption of the model (the physics changed under it)
``extrapolation``          the assumptions hold but the case is outside the training envelope
``numerical_resolution``   grid or time-step dependence (GCI, change under refinement), non-finite or out-of-
                           bounds values from an unresolved solution
``measurement``            the reference itself is suspect (sensor check), so the "error" may not be the model's
``missing_physics``        the model satisfies its own equations, inside its assumptions and envelope, and still
                           disagrees with the reference: its equations miss a mechanism (model-form error)
=========================  ==============================================================================

Each cause gets a score in [0, 1] from its evidence; the scores, plus an "unexplained" share when nothing points
anywhere, are normalised into probabilities. The confidence of the diagnosis is the top probability times the
fraction of evidence types that were actually available: a diagnosis made without a residual, an audit or a
reference says so. This is the point the residual alone cannot make: a low residual with a high error points to
``missing_physics`` or ``measurement``; a high residual says *that* something failed, the other evidence says *why*.

functions.name: attribute_failure
functions.sig: (*, validity: ValidityReport | None = None, audit: AssumptionAudit | None = None, error: float | None = None, error_tolerance: float = 0.05, residual_baseline: float | Mapping[str, float] | None = None, resolution: Mapping[str, float] | None = None, measurement_suspect: bool | None = None, spread: float | None = None, spread_tolerance: float = 0.1, missing_mechanisms: list[str] | None = None) -...
functions.doc:
Weigh the evidence of one case.

``validity``: the monitor's report; ``audit``: the model's assumption audit for this case; ``error``: relative
error against a reference when one exists (``error_tolerance`` marks it as failed); ``residual_baseline``: the
model's in-domain residual level (number, or {check name: level}), to tell a residual jump from a residual
that is just above an absolute tolerance; ``resolution``: grid or time-step evidence, any of ``{"gci": ...,
"gci_tol": ...}``, ``{"refinement_change": ..., "refinement_tol": ...}`` (relative change of the prediction
under refinement), ``{"cfl": ..., "cfl_max": ...}``; ``measurement_suspect``: the reading failed its sensor
check; ``spread``: ensemble disagreement (relative); ``missing_mechanisms``: from the knowledge graph, named in
the evidence of ``missing_physics``.

children.summary: Physics failure attribution: not only *that* a prediction is wrong (or suspect), but its probable cause, with the evidence and a confidence.

children.name: pinneapple_physics.physics_audit.improvement
children.doc:
Physics-guided model improvement: when no model is good enough, which experiment or change is worth most?

:func:`recommend` turns the diagnosis of one case (an :class:`~.attribution.Attribution`, optionally the
assumption audit and the knowledge graph) into ranked actions; :func:`improvement_plan` aggregates many cases (a
validation campaign, a week of operation) so the actions that fix the most frequent and most confident causes come
first. Each action says what to do, why (the evidence), the expected gain and the cost:

=========================  ===================================================================================
cause                      actions
=========================  ===================================================================================
``regime_change``          high-fidelity runs in the new regime; train or adapt a model for it; switch to a
                           model or equation that represents the missing mechanism (from the knowledge graph)
``extrapolation``          high-fidelity runs at and around the case (design points given); active learning
``pde_violation``          more collocation points or residual weight where it fails; hard constraints
``conservation``           conservation projection (``pinneapple_physics.conservation``) or a penalty in the loss
``boundary_condition``     check the boundary data; enforce the condition exactly (ansatz or projection)
``numerical_resolution``   refine the mesh or the time step; run a grid convergence study
``measurement``            check the sensor; keep the reading out of training and of the weights
``missing_physics``        add the missing term; fit a model-discrepancy correction; calibrate parameters
=========================  ===================================================================================

The gain and cost are ordinal (1 low .. 3 high), stated in the table ``ACTIONS`` below, not computed: they are a
reviewer's ranking aid, and the priority is ``probability * confidence * gain / cost``.

functions.name: design_points
functions.sig: (features: Mapping[str, float], spread: float = 0.15, n: int = 5, seed: int = 0, keys: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[dict[str, float]]
functions.doc:
High-fidelity design points at and around a case: the case itself, then ``n - 1`` points spread by ``spread``
(in decades for positive features) on a Latin hypercube.

functions.name: recommend
functions.sig: (attribution: Attribution, audit: AssumptionAudit | None = None, graph: PhysicsKnowledgeGraph | None = None, features: Mapping[str, float] | None = None, model: str | None = None, min_probability: float = 0.1) -> list[Recommendation]
functions.doc:
Ranked actions for one case. With ``graph``, ``model`` and ``features`` the "switch formulation" and "add
term" actions name the mechanism the model lacks and the models or equations that represent it; with
``features`` the high-fidelity actions list design points.

functions.name: improvement_plan
functions.sig: (cases: Iterable[Attribution | tuple[Attribution, list[Recommendation]]], top: int | None = None) -> list[Recommendation]
functions.doc:
Aggregate the recommendations of many cases: the same action summed over the cases that call for it (each
case's priority), so frequent, confident causes rank first. Items are attributions (recommended with
:func:`recommend` without context) or ``(attribution, recommendations)`` pairs.

children.summary: Physics-guided model improvement: when no model is good enough, which experiment or change is worth most?

children.name: pinneapple_physics.physics_audit.knowledge
children.doc:
Physics knowledge graph: phenomena, equations, assumptions, parameters, mechanisms and model families, and the
relations between them.

Nodes have a kind (``phenomenon``, ``equation``, ``assumption``, ``parameter``, ``mechanism``, ``model``); edges a
relation:

=====================  ===================================================================
``assumes``            equation or model -> assumption it rests on
``valid_when``         assumption -> parameter (with the condition, in the edge data)
``breaks_into``        assumption -> phenomenon that appears when it fails
``triggered_by``       phenomenon -> parameter (with the trigger condition)
``requires``           phenomenon -> mechanism a model needs to capture it
``uses``               model -> equation
``represents``         model or equation -> mechanism
=====================  ===================================================================

:func:`default_graph` builds the common fluid, heat and solid relations from the assumption catalogue. The queries the
router, the attribution and the improvement advisor use: :meth:`~PhysicsKnowledgeGraph.phenomena_triggered` (which
phenomena a case is in or near), :meth:`~PhysicsKnowledgeGraph.unrepresented` (triggered phenomena whose mechanism a
model lacks: "Re went up, is turbulence represented?"), :meth:`~PhysicsKnowledgeGraph.models_for` (models that
represent a mechanism) and :meth:`~PhysicsKnowledgeGraph.explain`. :meth:`~PhysicsKnowledgeGraph.to_mermaid` draws it.
Plain Python, no graph library needed.

methods.name: add_node
methods.sig: (id: str, kind: str, label: str = '', **data) -> Node

methods.name: add_edge
methods.sig: (src: str, rel: str, dst: str, **data) -> Edge

methods.name: add_phenomenon
methods.sig: (name: str, trigger: Condition | None, mechanism: str = '', description: str = '') -> None

methods.name: add_equation
methods.sig: (name: str, assumptions: Iterable[str | Assumption] = (), mechanisms: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None

methods.name: model_id
methods.doc: Models live in their own namespace, so a model may share a name with an assumption or an equation.

methods.name: add_model
methods.doc:
A model, its equations (added if new), its own assumptions (with its thresholds) and the mechanisms it
represents (given, plus those of its equations).

methods.name: out
methods.sig: (src: str, rel: str | None = None) -> list[Edge]

methods.name: into
methods.sig: (dst: str, rel: str | None = None) -> list[Edge]

methods.name: mechanisms_of
methods.doc: Mechanisms a model represents: its own plus those of the equations it uses.

methods.name: assumptions_of
methods.doc:
The model's own assumptions, then those of its equations it does not already state (a model's threshold
wins over the generic one of the same name).

methods.name: phenomena_triggered
methods.sig: (features: Mapping[str, float], include_marginal: bool = True) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
methods.doc: Phenomena whose trigger condition the case meets (or nearly meets, as ``MARGINAL``).

methods.name: unrepresented
methods.sig: (model: str, features: Mapping[str, float], generic: bool = True) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
methods.doc:
Phenomena the case is in (or near) whose mechanism ``model`` lacks: from the model's violated or marginal
assumptions (its own thresholds), then (``generic``) from the generic triggers, for numbers the model sets no
threshold on. The generic part needs the model to declare its mechanisms: without them nothing can be said.

functions.name: default_graph
functions.sig: (models: Iterable[ModelProfile] = ()) -> PhysicsKnowledgeGraph
functions.doc: The catalogue of assumptions, phenomena and equations above, plus ``models``.
